disposition_reason: Mean ± SD of 12 elements, including lead and mercury, for ten gourmet table salts bought in Messina, Italy.

study.origin: per Table 1 (Marsala, Iran, Guerande, Hawaii, Himalayas, Maldon, Palermo; two not stated)
study.market: local markets in Messina, southern Italy
study.method: 5 g salt in 100 mL water with 1 mL HNO3, 3 days, filtered; ICP-MS (iCAP-Q) for 11 elements; Hg by DMA-80 thermal decomposition amalgamation AAS
study.qa: addition-recovery tests at two levels: 91.36% (Ca) to 101.50% (Pb); no CRM

regulatory_or_exposure.what: text states lead exceeded the maximum level in all samples
element intake from 5 g salt per day

unresolved: Table 4 lists Hg average 0.00661 with MAX 0.00394, a maximum below the average; Table 3 shows 0.0394 for one salt.
Text says Hawaiian black salt had the highest aluminum, but Tables 3 and 5 put the highest aluminum (14.11 mg/Kg) in the Marsala sea salt.
Lead at 5-9 mg/Kg in all salts is far above other salt surveys in this corpus; the dissolution-only preparation and the cited LOD units (µg/Kg) are not discussed against this; values kept as printed.
The 'smoked salt' and 'Atlantic grey' origins are not stated; the figure suggests both North America and Northern Europe for smoked salt.
